meta.description: Caregiver / family-member external dose after discharge of a radionuclide-therapy patient: proximity profiles, evaluation criteria per category, references and model assumptions.
meta.origin: Port of the workbook Dosis_acompanantes_simple_v2.1.xlsx by José Ramón Sendón del Río (sheets Dosis, Curva and Comprobación).

kinetic_presets_note: Literature values describe a cohort, not the patient. Under each preset, «Spread in the source» gives the dispersion the source publishes, with its statistic named (mean ± SD, median with quartiles and range, or spread of literature values). It describes the cohort, not an interval for the patient: mean + 2 SD is only a reference high value. No SD is derived here from ranges or quartiles.

kinetic_presets.label: Lu-177-PSMA-617 — Demir (2016) / Kurth (2018)
kinetic_presets.source: Default preset. T fast 16.4 h is consistent with the mean dose rates at 1 m of Demir et al. (2016) Table 1, 15 µSv/h at 6 h and 7 µSv/h at 24 h: 18 h · ln 2 / ln(15/7) = 16.37 h. T slow 40.5 h: mean effective half-life after 48 h, Kurth et al. (2018) (cohort range 21.7–85.7 h). 6 cycles as in Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025).

spread.text: Dose rate at 1 m — Demir et al. (2016), Table 1, 23 patients, 7.4 GBq: 15 ± 4 µSv/h at 6 h and 7 ± 2 µSv/h at 24 h after infusion. Table 1 does not name the statistic after ±; the paper uses mean ± SD in its Table 3.

T fast: no dispersion published; 16.4 h is derived from the mean rates. With mean + 2 SD at both times (23 and 11 µSv/h): 18 h · ln 2 / ln(23/11) = 16.9 h, the «high» case among the self-check reference cases.

T slow — Kurth et al. (2018), Table 3, measurement at 48 h: 40.5 ± 15.8 h (mean ± SD), minimum 21.7 h, maximum 85.7 h (the T slow of that «high» reference case). The abstract prints «40.5 ± 9.6 h»: 9.6 h is the SD of the 72 h column (38.4 ± 9.6 h, 25.7–74.5 h, 25 patients), a discrepancy between abstract and table; Table 3 is followed. At 24 h: 26.0 ± 12.4 h (11.0–73.5 h).

kinetic_presets.label: Lu-177-PSMA-617 — Gayol Vilorio (2025)
kinetic_presets.source: Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025), Tables 4 and 6: Tef,1 = 22 h (median of the early mono-exponential fits, 12–24 h post-infusion, Table 2), Tef,2 = 42 h (median of the late values), 6 cycles; fast phase until 24 h post-infusion.

spread.text: No SD published: Tef,1 = 22 h is the median of two literature values, Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025), Table 2: early mono-exponential 18.5 h (Parlak) and 26 h (Kurth).

Tef,2 = 42 h is the median of seven literature values from five studies (late mono-exponential or slow bi-exponential), spread 38.4–54 h. Table 2 labels the 26 and 38.4 h of Kurth as medians; in Kurth et al. (2018), Table 3, they are means (24 h and 72 h). For the cohort SD see the Demir (2016) / Kurth (2018) preset.

kinetic_presets.label: Lu-177-DOTATATE — Gayol Vilorio (2025)
kinetic_presets.source: Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025), Tables 3 and 5: Tef,1 = 25 h (median of the early mono-exponential fits, Table 2), Tef,2 = 55 h (median of the late values), 4 cycles; fast phase until 24 h post-infusion.

spread.text: No SD published: Tef,1 = 25 h is the only early value in Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025), Table 2 (Monserrat); its cohort spread is given under the Monserrat preset.
Tef,2 = 55 h is the median of five literature values (late mono-exponential or slow bi-exponential), spread 49.5–58 h.

kinetic_presets.label: Lu-177-DOTATATE — Monserrat Fuertes (2023)
kinetic_presets.source: Monserrat Fuertes et al. (2023), Table 2, 20 patients: median Teff from the 6 h and 24 h values 25 h (range 12–92 h); median Teff from the 24, 48 and 168 h values 58 h (range 35–119 h); 4 cycles of 7.4 GBq. In that cohort patients were discharged at 24 h with a median rate at 1 m of 5.4 µSv/h.

spread.text: Teff from the 6 and 24 h values — Monserrat Fuertes et al. (2023), Table 2, 20 patients: 25 (12, 21, 36, 92) h, median (minimum, Q1, Q3, maximum).
Teff from the 24, 48 and 168 h values: 58 (35, 47, 67, 119) h, median (minimum, Q1, Q3, maximum). Neither half-life distribution is normal (Shapiro–Wilk), so no SD is given.
Dose rate at 1 m at discharge (24 h): 5.4 (2.4, 3.7, 6.5, 19.5) µSv/h, median (minimum, Q1, Q3, maximum). The ± of each patient in Table 2 is the uncertainty of the fit, not a cohort dispersion.

kinetic_presets.label: I-131 (NaI) — thyroid remnant ablation, Foro (2011)
kinetic_presets.source: Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.B, Table 3.B 3: «Tef (vida media efectiva) = 3 días», single exponential. In the Forum's equations Tef = 1/λ (mean life), so the effective half-life is 3 d · ln 2 = 49.9 h; with this reading the app reproduces Tables 3.B 3 and 3.B 4 (partner < 60 years, 2 mSv), with the half-life reading it does not. In-patients for 48–72 h.

kinetic_presets.label: I-131 (NaI) — thyroid cancer metastases, Foro (2011)
kinetic_presets.source: Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.B, Table 3.B 4: «T.ef. (vida media efectiva) = 5 días» = 1/λ, i.e. effective half-life 5 d · ln 2 = 83.2 h. Single exponential.

kinetic_presets.label: I-131 (NaI) — hyperthyroidism, Foro (2011)
kinetic_presets.source: Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.C, Table 3.C 2: «T.ef. (vida media efectiva) = 7,2 días», computed with the equation of Annex 3.B, where Tef = 1/λ: effective half-life 7.2 d · ln 2 = 119.8 h. Single exponential from discharge; the thyroid uptake peaks at 24–48 h, so early urinary excretion of an out-patient is not modelled. Usually out-patient; the Forum gives this table by administered activity (185–800 MBq), the app needs the rate measured at 1 m.

own.distances_note: Complete the own-measurement table (1 m row fixed by the discharge rate).

categories.label: Carer ≤ 60 years
categories.basis: EC RP 97 (1998), table 1, and Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), table 2: 3 mSv for adults up to 60 years — more restrictive than the international 5 mSv per episode (ICRP 103 [7], para. 351). RD 601/2019, arts. 6.2, 7 and 8, requires carer constraints but sets no value

categories.label: Carer > 60 years
categories.basis: ICRP 103 (2007), para. 351, and ICRP 94 (2004): 5 mSv per episode for carers; IAEA SSG-46 (2018), para. 2.49: usually 5 mSv per episode for adult carers, less severe constraints allowed for elderly people. Adopted by Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025) instead of the 15 mSv of EC RP 97 and the Forum

categories.label: Public (adult, child or pregnant woman)
categories.basis: RD 1029/2022, art. 15: public annual limit, applied to the whole treatment; ICRP 94 (2004) and ICRP 103, para. 351: the public limit applies to infants, children and casual visitors

categories.label: Co-worker
categories.basis: EC RP 97 (1998) and Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), table 2 (p. 13): 0.3 mSv for third persons

criteria_note: Evaluation criteria adopted in this application, not values fixed by regulation for this treatment. Scope: one person, the whole treatment (all cycles together) — the ICRP «episode» (the duration of a given release after therapy) is applied to the complete treatment, which is the more restrictive reading. Carers are people who, outside their occupation, knowingly and voluntarily help in the care of the patient (RD 601/2019, art. 7.1); children and pregnant women are assessed with the public category. The criterion only changes the comparison and the inverse calculations, never the calculated dose.
assumptions: Quantity: the integral of the measured operational quantity estimates the external exposure of the person; it is not automatically the individual effective dose nor the fetal dose. Internal contamination, the dose before discharge and other sources are not included.
Time model: two consecutive, continuous exponentials. At the end of the fast phase the rate reached is kept. It is not a simultaneous sum of components.

Occupancy h/24 is a daily average, not an exact timetable. Because the rate decreases, the dose of any timetable with the declared hours in every 24 h interval from discharge lies within the bounds given under the results (rate at the start or at the end of each interval); they are given only for restrictions of whole days. Close contact early in each interval makes the average underestimate the dose; the error repeats every day and does not cancel. The bounds widen as the half-life shortens, so they are widest in the fast phase and with an early discharge. Single trips and contacts concentrated during the fast phase still require a specific time-resolved assessment. For the period without restrictions, Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.A, eqs. (4) and (7), takes the rate at the start of each day, i.e. the upper bound.
Spatial factors are taken as constant in both phases. Body redistribution can change them: justify their use for the time of discharge and the case.
Equal cycles: same discharge rate, kinetics and cohabitation. Multiplying by the number of cycles assumes the pattern repeats with no relevant change from overlapping cycles.
Distances: keep the same origin, posture and orientation as the profile or measurement protocol. Do not confuse the separation between surfaces with the distance to a geometric centre.
Approximate profiles: published conventions, not universal measured factors. No automatic interpolation or extrapolation: the distance is chosen from the profile list.
Own measurements: enter distances and the rates at those distances, measured at the same time as the 1 m reading. Record the protocol. Do not repeat distances.

Discharge time and end of the fast phase are counted from administration. With the Kurth and Demir model the fast phase ends at 24 h. If discharge is later (or the end is 0) only the slow half-life is used, and the discharge rate must already belong to the slow phase.
Each cycle is integrated to infinity: with several weeks between cycles, practically the whole dose of a cycle is received before the next one.
Restriction days are counted from discharge. The criterion covers only the administrations entered; it does not by itself demonstrate annual compliance.
inverse_note: Maximum rate: the discharge rate that exactly exhausts the criterion with the restrictions of the table (the dose is proportional to the rate). Minimum restriction: days that exhaust the criterion applying the same duration to both rows; "Unattainable" = not met however long it lasts: contact during the restriction must be reduced. To apply it, enter the adopted restriction in the days column of the cohabitation table.
own_protocol_note: Own-measurement protocol to record: radiopharmaceutical, distance reference, posture, orientation and time of measurement.
references: [1] Monserrat Fuertes et al. (2023). Individualisation of radiation protection recommendations for patients treated with [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE. EJNMMI Physics 10:50. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40658-023-00570-7 — proximity factors (medians of measurements at 0.1, 0.5 and 1 m) and DOTATATE kinetics.

[2] Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011). Criterios de alta de pacientes y medidas para la protección radiológica del público después de tratamientos metabólicos con I-131 — contact taken at 0.4 m, I-131 kinetics, 3 mSv and 0.3 mSv criteria.

[3] Gayol Vilorio et al. (2025). Cálculo del periodo de restricciones tras el alta radiológica de pacientes sometidos a terapia metabólica con [177Lu]Lu-DOTA-TATE y [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. Rev. Fís. Méd. 26(2):27–36 — Lu-177 kinetics, contact at 0.4 m, 5 mSv over 60 years.

[4] Demir et al. (2016). Evaluation of radiation safety in 177Lu-PSMA therapy and outpatient treatment protocol. J. Radiol. Prot. 36(2):269. https://doi.org/10.1088/0952-4746/36/2/269 — dose rates at 1 m (PSMA fast phase).
[5] Kurth et al. (2018). External radiation exposure, excretion and effective half-life in 177Lu-PSMA-targeted therapies. EJNMMI Research 8:32 — slow effective half-life; fast phase ending at 24 h.
[6] ICRP Publication 94 (2004). Release of patients after therapy with unsealed radionuclides — 5 mSv per episode for relatives and caregivers; public limit for infants, children and casual visitors.
[7] ICRP Publication 103 (2007), para. 351 — 5 mSv per episode (the duration of a given release after therapy) for carers other than young children, used flexibly.
[8] IAEA SSG-46 (2018), para. 2.49 — usually 5 mSv per episode for adult carers; less severe constraints allowed for elderly people.
[9] European Commission, Radiation Protection 97 (1998), table 1 — I-131: children 1 mSv, adults up to 60 years 3 mSv, over 60 years 15 mSv; third persons 0.3 mSv.
[10] IAEA Safety Reports Series No. 63 (2009). Release of patients after radionuclide therapy — 5 mSv during the treatment (1996 BSS); Appendix II, limits of the inverse square law at short distance.

reference_cases.note: Reference cases computed with the author's original spreadsheet: restriction 3 d from discharge, 6 cycles, fast phase ending at 24 h. Carer: 6 h/d at 1 m during the restriction; afterwards 6 h/d at 1 m and 8 h/d in contact (factor 6.25) → fr = 0.25, fn = 2.3333. Non-carer adult: 6 h/d at 1 m with no shared rest → fr = fn = 0.25. Expected values rounded to 2 decimals.

profiles_note: The intermediate distances of the approximate profiles [2], [3] are model evaluations, not measurements, and 6.25 is not a measured ratio: the spatial ratios measured by Demir [4] vary with time. The d^-1.5 approximation of IAEA SRS-63 [10] is not adopted as a universal profile.
kinetic_presets_no_spread: No dispersion published: the source gives a single fixed value.

cohabitation_scenarios.label: Partner
cohabitation_scenarios.normal: 6 hours at 1 metre, 8 hours at 0.1 m
cohabitation_scenarios.note: Day-time contact continues during the restriction.

cohabitation_scenarios.label: Child under 1 year
cohabitation_scenarios.normal: 6 periods of 30 minutes at 0.1 metre and 3 hours at 0.5 metres
cohabitation_scenarios.restriction: 3 hours at 1.5 metres or not living in the same home
cohabitation_scenarios.note: Not living in the same home: enter 0 h during the restriction in both rows.

cohabitation_scenarios.label: Child 1 to 2 years
cohabitation_scenarios.normal: 4 periods of 25 minutes at 0.1 metre and 3 hours at 0.5 metres
cohabitation_scenarios.restriction: 3 hours at 1.5 metres or not living in the same home
cohabitation_scenarios.note: 4 × 25 min = 1.667 h. Not living in the same home: enter 0 h during the restriction in both rows.

cohabitation_scenarios.label: Child 2 to 5 years
cohabitation_scenarios.normal: 2 hours at 0.1 metre and 5 hours at 1 metre
cohabitation_scenarios.restriction: 5 hours at 1.5 metres or not living in the same home
cohabitation_scenarios.note: Not living in the same home: enter 0 h during the restriction in both rows.

cohabitation_scenarios.label: Child 5 to 11 years
cohabitation_scenarios.normal: 1 hour at 0.1 metre and 5 hours at 1 metre

cohabitation_scenarios.label: Child over 11 years
cohabitation_scenarios.normal: 1 hour at 0.1 metre and 4 hours at 1 metre
cohabitation_scenarios.note: Children of any age: public criterion (1 mSv), a choice of this application. Table 2 of the Forum gives 3 mSv over 10 years, but its own Tables 3.B 3 and 3.B 4 are closer to 1 mSv for this column.

cohabitation_scenarios.label: Co-worker
cohabitation_scenarios.normal: 8 hours at 1 metre from the co-worker
cohabitation_scenarios.note: A pregnant co-worker is assessed individually (distances and times): use the free scenario.

cohabitation_scenarios.label: Work with children (nurseries, childminders)
cohabitation_scenarios.normal: 3 hours at 1 metre, 3 hours at 0.1 m
cohabitation_scenarios.note: Criterion for the children cared for: the Forum applies the co-worker constraint (0.3 mSv), which is below the public one.

cohabitation_note: A scenario fills the hours and distances of both rows and proposes the category; it never changes the restriction days. The free scenario keeps the table as it is and lets you name the rows, for cases the Forum does not cover (a pregnant co-worker, other timetables or other people). Source: Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.B, Table 3.B 1 and the paragraph «Para compañeros de trabajo» (p. 29); the 0.3 mSv for co-workers comes from its section 4.6.

cohabitation_method.source: Foro CSN-SEPR-SEFM (2011), Annex 3.B, Table 3.B 1 «Condiciones de convivencia sin y con restricciones para familiares y personas que cuidan al paciente (periodos diarios)» and the paragraph that follows it (p. 29). Daily periods.
coworkers: For co-workers, a stay of 8 hours at one metre from the co-worker is assumed. If a co-worker is pregnant, the conditions (distances and times) are assessed individually when the restriction period is calculated.
Work with children (nurseries, childminders): 3 hours at 1 metre, 3 hours at 0.1 m.

Since the inverse square law does not hold at short distances, for the calculation the dose rate at 0.1 m, which would be contact, is taken as the one at 0.4 m. The restriction in this case consists in not going to work during the period indicated.
Co-workers should not exceed the dose constraint of 0.3 mSv (section 4.6). Food handlers (Table 3.B 2) are an internal-contamination pathway of consumers and are not modelled here.
cohabitation_method.reproduction: Check with the app (I-131 presets, Tef = 1/λ, contact at 0.4 m, days rounded to the nearest integer): with the conditions of Table 3.B 1 it reproduces all 16 cells of Tables 3.B 3 and 3.B 4 for the partner under 60 (2 mSv), children under 1, 2–5 and 5–11 years (1 mSv) and general work (0.3 mSv). It does not reproduce, as printed, the columns over 11 years (2 cells differ with 1 mSv, 5 with 3 mSv), 1–2 years (8 cells) and work with children (1 cell: 6.49 d against 7 at 40 µSv/h, Tef 3 d). The tables state «condiciones en Rivas 2002», which may differ from Table 3.B 1; with several free parameters no other set of conditions can be identified conclusively, so Table 3.B 1 is used as printed.
